rows.source: HSE grid-scale battery energy storage
rows.verified: Battery-energy-storage health-and-safety duties apply across the system life cycle, including design, installation and operation.

rows.source: HSE grid-scale battery energy storage
rows.verified: Employers must manage BESS risks to employees, other workers and members of the public under general health-and-safety law.

rows.source: HSE grid-scale battery energy storage
rows.verified: Dangerous-substances rules establish minimum controls for fire and explosion risks associated with relevant BESS hazards.

rows.source: HSE grid-scale battery energy storage
rows.verified: Electrical-safety law requires precautions against death or personal injury from electrical work activities.

rows.source: HSE grid-scale battery energy storage
rows.verified: Management regulations require BESS risks to be assessed and appropriately managed.

rows.source: HSE grid-scale battery energy storage
rows.verified: Construction-design-and-management duties apply so that the project is planned and carried out with health and safety secured.

rows.source: HSE grid-scale battery energy storage
rows.verified: Operators holding at least 25 tonnes of dangerous substances may have to notify the local fire and rescue service and display site signs.

rows.source: HSE grid-scale battery energy storage
rows.verified: Planning permission and environmental permitting questions are handled through the relevant planning and environmental authorities.

rows.source: HSE grid-scale battery energy storage
rows.verified: BESS risk depends on battery chemistry, state of charge, capacity, enclosure, thermal management, electrical design, location and emergency response.

rows.source: HSE grid-scale battery energy storage
rows.verified: BESS evidence is technology-, installation-, operating-, location- and incident-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire or explosion probability.

rows.source: HSE outdoor workers and sun exposure
rows.verified: Ultraviolet radiation from sunlight can damage skin, and a tan indicates that skin damage has occurred.

rows.source: HSE outdoor workers and sun exposure
rows.verified: Workers who spend long periods outdoors can receive more ultraviolet exposure than is healthy.

rows.source: HSE outdoor workers and sun exposure
rows.verified: Even mild skin reddening is evidence of sun damage, while more severe exposure can cause blistering and peeling.

rows.source: HSE outdoor workers and sun exposure
rows.verified: Long-term excessive sunlight can accelerate skin ageing and increase the risk of skin cancer.

rows.source: HSE outdoor workers and sun exposure
rows.verified: Outdoor workers should cover exposed skin where practical and wear a hat that protects the head, ears and neck.

rows.source: HSE outdoor workers and sun exposure
rows.verified: Shade should be used during breaks, particularly around the middle of the day when exposure can be intense.

rows.source: HSE outdoor workers and sun exposure
rows.verified: HSE advises using high-factor sunscreen on exposed skin alongside clothing and shade rather than as the only control.

rows.source: HSE outdoor workers and sun exposure
rows.verified: Outdoor-work arrangements should include drinking water, rest breaks and awareness of heat-stress and dehydration symptoms.

rows.source: HSE outdoor workers and sun exposure
rows.verified: Sun and outdoor-work risk depends on UV intensity, season, duration, skin type, clothing, shade, workload, heat and hydration.

rows.source: HSE outdoor workers and sun exposure
rows.verified: Sun-exposure evidence is person-, weather-, task-, season- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level skin-cancer probability.
